axiom-ai--coreml-compression.content:
# Core ML Compression (QAT vs PTQ)

Shrinking a custom Core ML model to fit memory and run fast on device. Dominant decision: **post-training quantization (PTQ)** vs **quantization-aware training (QAT)**. After conversion (`coreml-conversion.md`), before deployment (`skills/coreml-deployment.md`). API signatures and code → `coreml-ref.md` Part 6.

## When to Use

- Converted model too large or too slow → quantize / palettize / prune
- Accuracy dropped more than acceptable after compressing
- Cheap post-training pass enough, or retrain?

## The Core Decision: PTQ vs QAT

| | Post-training (PTQ) | Quantization-aware training (QAT) |
|--|---------------------|-----------------------------------|
| **When applied** | After training | During training (low precision simulated in the loss) |
| **Cost** | Minutes, no retraining, often data-free | Full retraining loop with QAT-aware optimizers |
| **Accuracy hit** | Larger — worse on small models, low bit-widths, sensitive tasks | Smaller — weights learned robust to quantization |
| **coremltools module** | `optimize.coreml` (on the `.mlpackage`) **or** `optimize.torch` (on the PyTorch model) | `optimize.torch` (hooks into the PyTorch training loop) |

Rubric:
0. Profile the Float16 baseline first. Size ≈ Float16 × nbits/16, plus LUT/scale overhead (8-bit ≈ ½, WWDC 2024-10159).
1. **PTQ** first — free. Step bit-width down 8 → 6 → 4 (`per_grouped_channel`), measuring accuracy at each step.
2. Accuracy holds at the target bit-width → ship.
3. Degrades too much (common at int4 / sub-4-bit, or small models) → **calibration PTQ** (data sample), then **QAT**.
4. QAT can't hold it → bit-width too aggressive; back off.

Authority: Apple ships its on-device foundation model at **2 bits per weight using QAT** (arXiv 2507.13575), balanced 2-bit set `{-1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5}` chosen because it trained more smoothly than `{-2, -1, 0, 1}`. Lesson: Apple reached for QAT, not PTQ, to survive aggressive quantization. 2-bit PTQ on a custom model almost always falls apart.

## Tiers and Families

| Tier | Needs | Module |
|---|---|---|
| Data-free PTQ | nothing | `optimize.coreml` on the `.mlpackage` (all three families), or `optimize.torch` post-training classes |
| Calibration PTQ | sample data | `optimize.torch` (all three families); `optimize.coreml.linear_quantize_activations` (8-bit activations only → W8A8) |
| QAT | training loop | `optimize.torch` (all three families) |

"Post-training" ≠ "`optimize.coreml`": `optimize.torch` holds data-free PTQ, calibration PTQ, and QAT. Class per tier × family → `coreml-ref.md` Part 6.

- **Palettization** — weights clustered into an N-bit lookup table; usually the best size/accuracy trade-off; `nbits` ∈ `{1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8}`
- **Quantization** — linear int8 / int4 weights, optional int8 activations; W8A8 runs on the Neural Engine (A17 Pro+, M4)
- **Pruning** — zero low-magnitude weights (magnitude threshold, target sparsity, block-structured, N:M). Composes with either: sparse-palettized / sparse-quantized.
  - **Stacking two `optimize.coreml` passes needs `joint_compression=True` on the second call** (prune → palettize/quantize, palettize → quantize, quantize → prune). Without it the second pass is silently skipped: no error, no warning, only the first compression ships (measured, coremltools 9.0) → `coreml-ref.md` Part 6

## Deployment Target and Hardware Fit

| Method | Suits (WWDC 2024-10159) |
|---|---|
| `per_grouped_channel` palettization | Neural Engine |
| int4 or `per_block` quantization | Mac GPUs |
| joint: sparse + palettized/quantized | Neural Engine |

All three need `minimum_deployment_target` ≥ `ct.target.iOS18`, as do vector palettization (`cluster_dim > 1`) and `enable_per_channel_scale`. Below iOS 18 the compression call raises `ValueError`, e.g. `The per_grouped_channel palettization is supported since iOS18. Please re-convert your model with minimum_deployment_target set to at least ct.target.iOS18.` (same shape for vector palettization, 4-bit, `per_block`, joint; `enable_per_channel_scale` reads `Palettization with per-channel-scale is only supported since iOS18…`). Fix at conversion: at least `iOS18`; use your app's minimum OS (`ct.target.iOS26` for a 26+ app) → `coreml-conversion.md`. iOS 16 methods (per-tensor palettization, per-channel int8, sparsity) and the full matrix → `coreml-ref.md` Part 9.

## Always Re-Measure After Compressing

Lossy by definition → eval set before and after every pass, on a realistic input distribution. Fine on synthetic inputs can collapse on real ones. Most-skipped step; most expensive to discover in production. Locating the damaged op → `coreml-diag.md` (Accuracy Loss After Compression).

## Boundary

- QAT/PTQ = deployment-stage decisions for custom Core ML models you train or convert
- Apple's Foundation Models are already 2-bit-quantized at the framework level → you don't quantize them; FM adapters are LoRA deltas inheriting the base quantization → `axiom-ai`

## Anti-Rationalization

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "Compression is free accuracy savings" | Lossy, PTQ especially → re-measure on real inputs; accuracy can drop silently |
| "PTQ is enough, QAT is overkill" | True at int8 on big models; false at int4/sub-4-bit or small models. Apple needed QAT for 2-bit → match method to bit-width |
| "2-bit worked for Apple, I'll do 2-bit PTQ" | Apple used 2-bit *QAT* with a hand-tuned weight set and recovery adapters → 2-bit PTQ on a custom model almost certainly fails |
| "I'll quantize Apple's Foundation Model to save space" | Already 2-bit at the framework level → this page is for *your* models |
| "Pruning or quantization, pick one" | They compose (second pass with `joint_compression=True`) and often beat either alone |

## Resources

**WWDC**: 2024-10159

**Docs**: coremltools 9.0 guide at apple.github.io/coremltools (`opt-overview`, `opt-quantization-api`, `opt-palettization-api`, `opt-pruning-api`); Apple Intelligence Foundation Language Models Tech Report 2025 (arXiv 2507.13575) for the 2-bit QAT specifics

**Skills**: coreml-conversion (produce the model first), coreml-deployment (run the compressed model), coreml-ref (optimize API index), `skills/ios-ml.md` (hub), coreml-training (train from scratch / personalize), axiom-ai (Foundation Models — already quantized)

axiom-ai--coreml-conversion.content:
# Core ML Conversion (coremltools)

Already-trained PyTorch / TensorFlow / Keras model → Core ML with the Python `coremltools` package. Doesn't train (`coreml-training.md`), compress (`coreml-compression.md`), or update anything.

## When to Use

- `.pt` / TorchScript / `torch.export` PyTorch model, or TensorFlow/Keras SavedModel → need a `.mlpackage` to ship
- Conversion "succeeded" but Core ML outputs don't match the source
- `coremltools` import or op-support errors → version mismatch or unsupported layer?

## Boundary

| Intent | Go to |
|--------|-------|
| Convert a trained PyTorch/TF model to Core ML | This page |
| Shrink the converted model (quantize / palettize / prune) | `coreml-compression.md` |
| Train a new model from scratch | `coreml-training.md` (Create ML) |
| Personalize a deployed model on-device | `coreml-training.md` (`MLUpdateTask`) |
| Fine-tune Apple's on-device LLM | `foundation-models-adapters.md` |
| Deploy / run the converted model | `skills/coreml-deployment.md` |

Producing the weights = training, not conversion.

## The Unified Converter

One entry point: `coremltools.convert(model, ...)`; output format set by `convert_to` / `minimum_deployment_target`:

- `.mlpackage` (ML Program, `"mlprogram"`) — default; use for anything new
- `.mlmodel` (NeuralNetwork, `"neuralnetwork"`) — legacy NN-spec; only when NN-spec is required, e.g. on-device personalization via `MLUpdateTask` (NN-spec-only → `coreml-training.md`)

```python
import coremltools as ct

mlmodel = ct.convert(
    traced_model,                              # source model (see capture modes below)
    convert_to="mlprogram",                    # default; "neuralnetwork" only for NN-spec needs
    minimum_deployment_target=ct.target.iOS26, # pin to the OS you actually ship
    compute_precision=ct.precision.FLOAT16,    # FP16 is the default; set FLOAT32 only if accuracy demands
    inputs=[ct.TensorType(name="x", shape=(1, 3, 224, 224))],
)
mlmodel.save("Model.mlpackage")
```

### Supported source formats

| Source | Status |
|--------|--------|
| PyTorch | TorchScript (`torch.jit.trace`) — stable, production default; `torch.export` (ExportedProgram) — beta, since coremltools 8 |
| TensorFlow 1.x / 2.x | frozen graph, SavedModel, concrete functions |
| Keras | via the TensorFlow path (`tf.keras.Model`, `.h5`) |
| ONNX | **Removed** (`onnx-coreml` frozen, unmaintained) → convert ONNX → PyTorch or TF first |
| JAX | not a direct source → `jax2tf` → TF → Core ML |

### PyTorch capture: trace vs export

- `torch.jit.trace` — stable default; traces one forward pass → data-dependent control flow not captured
- `torch.export.export` — coremltools 8+, beta; preferred long-term → verify parity before relying on it
- Either way: concrete `inputs` (`ct.TensorType` / `ct.ImageType`); variable sizes → `ct.RangeDim` or `ct.EnumeratedShapes`

### Choosing `minimum_deployment_target`

At least `ct.target.iOS18`; use your app's minimum OS (`ct.target.iOS26` for a 26+ app), not the newest SDK — it gates your install base. Conversion-relevant gates:

| Target | Unlocks at conversion |
|---|---|
| iOS 18 | `states=` (stateful models); fused `scaled_dot_product_attention` op instead of matmul/softmax pieces (WWDC 2024-10159: "really shines on Apple Silicon GPUs"); grouped-channel/per-block/int4/joint compression (`coreml-compression.md`) |
| iOS 26 | int8 model inputs/outputs |

Full matrix (iOS 15–27, runtime + coremltools) → `coreml-ref.md` Part 9.

### Stateful models — KV-cache (iOS 18+)

- PyTorch side: `register_buffer("keyCache", …)`; update in place inside `forward`; caches are not `forward` inputs
- `states=[ct.StateType(...)]`, with `name` set to the buffer name (`named_buffers()` key); state is fp16 ("As of iOS 18, Core ML state can only be fp16", coremltools source)
- Wrapped `TensorType` takes no `name`/`default_value`; `StateType` inside `inputs` raises `ValueError`; PyTorch sources only (`'states' can only be passed with pytorch source model.`)

```python
import numpy as np
import coremltools as ct

cache_shape = (1, 32, 2048, 128)
mlmodel = ct.convert(
    traced_model,
    inputs=[ct.TensorType(name="inputIds", shape=(1, ct.RangeDim(1, 2048)), dtype=np.int32)],
    states=[
        ct.StateType(wrapped_type=ct.TensorType(shape=cache_shape, dtype=np.float16), name="keyCache"),
        ct.StateType(wrapped_type=ct.TensorType(shape=cache_shape, dtype=np.float16), name="valueCache"),
    ],
    minimum_deployment_target=ct.target.iOS18,
)
```

Runtime (`makeState()`, serialization rules) → `coreml-deployment.md`.

### Converting an already-compressed source

- Compressed with `coremltools.optimize.torch` → compression metadata (`_COREML_…` state-dict keys) read automatically, only when `minimum_deployment_target` ≥ iOS 16
- Weights already palettized or sparse by other means → `pass_pipeline=ct.PassPipeline.DEFAULT_PALETTIZATION` / `DEFAULT_PRUNING` emits the compressed format
- Adapter variants of one base → convert each, merge into one multifunction `.mlpackage` (`coreml-deployment.md`)

## Always Validate Parity

A successful convert only means the graph lowered. Same representative inputs → source model and Core ML model → compare outputs (max abs/relative error; classifiers: top-k agreement). Real input distribution, not random noise.

## Failure Modes

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| `NotImplementedError: PyTorch convert function for op 'X' not implemented.` | No MIL lowering for `X` | Upgrade coremltools; rewrite with supported ops (coremltools op-support list); or `@register_torch_op` from `coremltools.converters.mil` (not `mb.`) |
| Same, plus `Dynamic quantized models are not supported by Core ML.` | PyTorch dynamic quantization | Convert the float model, then compress with `coremltools.optimize` (`coreml-compression.md`) |
| Converts; outputs diverge on every compute unit | Preprocessing (`ct.ImageType` `scale`/`bias`/`color_layout`), training-mode layers, precision drop, imperfect op mapping | Parity check above; compare layer-level outputs; `compute_precision=ct.precision.FLOAT32` separates precision from op mapping |
| Correct on `CPU_ONLY`, wrong on GPU/NE | One op's FP16 precision | `coreml-diag.md` (Wrong Output on One Compute Unit) |
| `coremltools` import errors (e.g. `libmilstoragepython`) | `coremltools` / source-framework version mismatch | coremltools 9.0 is tested up to PyTorch 2.7.0 and TensorFlow 2.12.0 (newer → warning); `optimize.torch` needs PyTorch ≥ 2.1.0; pin in a clean venv |
| Tracing warns about control flow | `torch.jit.trace` can't capture data-dependent branches | `torch.export`, or script the dynamic submodule |

## Anti-Rationalization

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "Conversion succeeded, so the model is correct" | Graph lowered ≠ outputs match → validate parity on representative inputs before shipping |
| "I'll just convert my ONNX model directly" | ONNX path removed → ONNX → PyTorch/TF first; skip `onnx-coreml` |
| "FP32 to be safe" | FP16 is the default and usually fine on Apple Silicon; FP32 doubles size and memory → measure accuracy first |
| "I'll target the latest OS so I get all the features" | `minimum_deployment_target` gates your install base → your app's minimum OS |
| "Trace and export are interchangeable" | Trace stable; `torch.export` beta in coremltools → trace for production unless export parity is verified |

## Resources

**WWDC**: 2024-10159

**Docs**: /coreml (runtime side); coremltools 9.0 guide at apple.github.io/coremltools (Unified Conversion API, `convert-pytorch-workflow`)

**Skills**: coreml-compression (shrink the converted model), coreml-training (Create ML / `MLUpdateTask`), coreml-deployment (run it in the app), coreml-ref (coremltools index), `skills/ios-ml.md` (hub), axiom-ai (Foundation Models), axiom-apple-docs

axiom-ai--coreml-diag.description: Runtime failures of your own Core ML models (`MLModel`, `.mlpackage` compiled to `.mlmodelc`). Diagnose here; fixes live in `coreml-deployment.md` (load, prewarm, concurrency, state), `coreml-ref.md` (API), `coreml-conversion.md` (convert, parity), `coreml-compression.md` (PTQ → calibration → QAT). `.aimodel` / `AIModel` → `core-ai.md`.
axiom-ai--coreml-diag.content:
# Core ML Diagnostics

Runtime failures of your own Core ML models (`MLModel`, `.mlpackage` compiled to `.mlmodelc`). Diagnose here; fixes live in `coreml-deployment.md` (load, prewarm, concurrency, state), `coreml-ref.md` (API), `coreml-conversion.md` (convert, parity), `coreml-compression.md` (PTQ → calibration → QAT). `.aimodel` / `AIModel` → `core-ai.md`.

## Red Flags

- Branching on `MLModelError.Code.io` for load failures. Core ML's own load errors arrive as `.generic` (code 0); the cause is only in `localizedDescription`. Measured, macOS 27.2: missing file and `.mlpackage` URL both `.generic`.
- Timing or compute-unit placement taken from the Simulator. iOS 27.0 Simulator: `availableComputeDevices` = simulator GPU + CPU, **no Neural Engine** (measured).
- `computeUnits = .cpuOnly` shipped as the fix. It is an isolation probe; it forfeits GPU and NE.
- `.mlpackage` URL passed to `MLModel.load` or `MLComputePlan.load`. Both take `.mlmodelc`. `MLComputePlan.load` on an `.mlpackage` **aborts the process** (uncaught C++ `ios_base::failure`: "It is not a valid .mlmodelc file") instead of throwing (measured, macOS 27.2).
- `MLModelAsset.modelDescription(of:)` with a name not in `functionNames` — including `"main"` on a single-function model (`functionNames` = `[]`) — **aborts the process** (uncaught `NSInvalidArgumentException`: "The specified function name: X is not among the available function names: [...]") instead of throwing (measured, macOS 27.2). Check `functionNames` first.
- "NE never used" on a model converted with `compute_precision=ct.precision.FLOAT32`. Float32-typed ML Programs are barred from the Neural Engine.
- `.all` read as "runs on NE". Core ML picks per op: a small linear model on M1 Max preferred CPU for every op under `.all` though NE supported them (measured). Read `preferred`, not `supported`.
- "Smaller on disk = smaller in RAM." Backend-dependent; some backends decompress weights fully before running.

## First Steps

1. Load threw → log `error.localizedDescription`, match **Load Failures**.
2. Profile on a device. Xcode 27.1 ships the Core ML instrument but **no Core ML template**; add it by name:

```bash
xcrun xctrace record --template 'Time Profiler' --instrument 'Core ML' --instrument 'Neural Engine' --instrument 'GPU' --device <UDID> --attach <AppName>
```

3. Separate `Load` intervals from `Prediction` intervals before optimizing either.
4. Per-op placement on the device (compiled `.mlmodelc` URL):

```swift
import CoreML

func logComputePlan(compiledModelURL: URL, computeUnits: MLComputeUnits = .all) async throws {
    print("Core ML devices:", MLModel.availableComputeDevices)
    let configuration = MLModelConfiguration()
    configuration.computeUnits = computeUnits
    let plan = try await MLComputePlan.load(contentsOf: compiledModelURL, configuration: configuration)
    guard case let .program(program) = plan.modelStructure,
          let main = program.functions["main"] else { return }
    for operation in main.block.operations {
        guard let usage = plan.deviceUsage(for: operation) else { continue }
        let cost = plan.estimatedCost(of: operation)?.weight ?? 0
        print(operation.operatorName, "preferred:", usage.preferred, "supported:", usage.supported, "cost:", cost)
    }
}
```

`cost` = share of total model work, 0–1. No-code equivalent: Xcode → open model → Performance tab → **+** → device → compute units → Run Test. Per op: filled check = ran there, empty diamond = unsupported there; hover an unsupported op for the reason. Same plan from Python: `ct.models.compute_plan.MLComputePlan.load_from_path(path, compute_units)` — reflects the Mac's hardware, not the phone's.

## Decision Tree

```dot
digraph coreml_diag {
    "Symptom?" [shape=diamond];
    "Wrong output?" [shape=diamond];
    "Symptom?" -> "Load Failures" [label="load throws"];
    "Symptom?" -> "Slow First Load" [label="first load slow,\nlater fast"];
    "Symptom?" -> "Slow Every Prediction" [label="every prediction slow"];
    "Symptom?" -> "Device or Simulator Differences" [label="differs on one device\nor in Simulator"];
    "Symptom?" -> "Memory Grows During Predictions" [label="memory climbs\nwhile predicting"];
    "Symptom?" -> "Memory Spike at Load" [label="spike or jetsam\nat load"];
    "Symptom?" -> "Wrong output?" [label="wrong output"];
    "Wrong output?" -> "Wrong Output on One Compute Unit" [label="CPU_ONLY right,\nGPU/NE wrong"];
    "Wrong output?" -> "Accuracy Loss After Compression" [label="only after\ncompression"];
    "Wrong output?" -> "coreml-conversion.md parity" [label="wrong on every unit"];
    "Symptom?" -> "Accuracy Loss After Compression" [label="compression didn't\nshrink or apply"];
    "Symptom?" -> "coreml-conversion.md failure modes" [label="ct.convert fails"];
    "Symptom?" -> "core-ai.md" [label=".aimodel / AIModel"];
}
```

## Load Failures

| `localizedDescription` | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| ``Unable to load model: <url>. Compile the model with Xcode or `MLModel.compileModel(at:)`.`` | URL is `.mlpackage`/`.mlmodel`; loaders take `.mlmodelc` | Bundle via Xcode (compiles at build), or `compileModel(at:)` → `coreml-deployment.md` |
| `The model is not found at URL: <url>` | Wrong URL; or a `compileModel(at:)` result left where it was written (a temporary location; measured `NSTemporaryDirectory()`) and later gone | Apple: save the compiled model to a permanent location such as Application Support; reload that path |
| `The specification version for compiled model is X and is more recent than the supported version Y.` / `The compiler version for compiled model is X and is more recent than this framework major version Y.` | `.mlmodelc` compiled by a newer toolchain/OS than the device | Ship `.mlpackage` and `compileModel(at:)` on device, or compile with an older deployment target |
| `The model specification version (N) is greater than the maximum supported version (M)` | Model spec newer than the OS's Core ML | Re-convert with `minimum_deployment_target` ≤ oldest supported OS |
| `Failed to build the model execution plan using a model architecture file '<path>' with error code: N.` / `Failed to configure the model to use CPU and NeuralEngine due to error code: N.` | Device-side plan build failed for this configuration; codes undocumented | Isolate: reload with `.cpuOnly`. Loads → a GPU/NE backend rejects an op: Performance report hover hint or compute plan `supported`. Still fails → re-convert with current coremltools |
| `` `MLModelConfiguration`'s `.functionName` property must be `nil` unless the model type is ML Program. `` | `functionName` not among the model's functions; same message for single- and multifunction models, from `load(contentsOf:)`, `load(asset:)`, `MLComputePlan.load` (measured, macOS 27.2). Single-function ML Program: only `nil` or `"main"`; NeuralNetwork: only `nil`; multifunction: no `"main"` unless merged under that name | Check `try await MLModelAsset(url:).functionNames` first (`[]` = single-function); `nil` → default function |
| `.featureType` | Input type differs from model input (e.g. image to `MLMultiArray` input) | Match `modelDescription.inputDescriptionsByName` |
| `.modelDecryptionKeyFetch` / `.modelDecryption` | Key-server network failure / key-server configuration | Retry on network; configuration is server-side |
| `.predictionCancelled` | Async prediction honored `Task` cancellation | Expected; don't surface as an error |

Version checks:
- Package: `ct.utils.load_spec("Model.mlpackage").specificationVersion`. `ct.target.iOS26` = 10, the newest coremltools 9.0 emits. A 26+ app loads any spec ≤ 10; version errors mean a newer toolchain's model reached an older OS (usually a downloaded model).
- Compiled: `jq '.[0].specificationVersion, .[0].availability' Model.mlmodelc/metadata.json`.
- Pre-rename numbers (measured, Xcode 27.1, spec-10 model): `metadata.json` `availability` reads `"iOS": "19.0"`, and the build-time check prints `This model is not supported on specified deployment target of iOS 18.0. It requires 19.0 or greater`. 19.0 = iOS 26. That check is a **warning**; the build succeeds and the load fails on the older OS.

## Slow First Load

Load labels (`Load (prepare and cache)` / `Load (cached)` / `Load`), cache key and invalidation → `coreml-deployment.md` (Load, Cache, Pre-Warm).

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `prepare and cache` every launch | Path or configuration changes between loads (e.g. recompiling to a fresh temp path each launch) | Compile once, permanent path, same `MLModelConfiguration` → `coreml-deployment.md` |
| `prepare and cache` after OS update or low disk | Expected invalidation | Prewarm before the user needs the model |
| Launch hang | Synchronous load at launch on the main thread | Apple: never load at launch on the UI thread; async `MLModel.load(contentsOf:configuration:)` or lazy load → `coreml-deployment.md` |
| Every prediction call shows a `Load` | Model reloaded per prediction | Keep one instance → `coreml-deployment.md` |

## Slow Every Prediction

| Cause | Evidence | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `computeUnits` pinned narrow | Configuration | Default `.all` (measured); narrow only after measuring |
| Op unsupported on NE/GPU → CPU fallback | Compute plan `preferred`; report hover hint | Apple's example hint was the data type: re-convert `compute_precision=ct.precision.FLOAT16` → `coreml-conversion.md` |
| Float32-typed model | `metadata.json` `computePrecision` = `"Float32"`; anything else is not Float32-typed (FP16 strings vary: `"Mixed (Float16, Float32)"`, `"Mixed (Float16, Float32, Int32)"`) → match on "not `Float32`" | Float32 bars NE; convert FLOAT16 |
| Compute-unit handoffs | `Neural Engine - Data Copy`, `Input Copy` intervals; NE→GPU handoff in NE instrument | IOSurface-backed buffers move data between units without copies → `coreml-ref.md` (`outputBackings`) |
| Input shape changes per call | Variable shapes; `optimizationHints.reshapeFrequency` default `.frequent` skips shape-specific optimization | Stable shapes → `.infrequent`; else `ct.EnumeratedShapes` at conversion. API → `coreml-ref.md` Part 1 |
| Latency-bound, load time affordable | — | `optimizationHints.specializationStrategy = .fastPrediction`; costs specialization time, memory, disk |
| Prediction or load on the main actor | Main-thread time in Time Profiler | Move into the actor or `@concurrent` job that owns the model (`MLModel` isn't Sendable) → `coreml-deployment.md` |
| Transformer decode re-feeds full history | Latency grows per token | Stateful KV-cache → `coreml-deployment.md`; LLM-scale → `core-ai.md` |
| Timing includes load | `Load` interval inside the measured span | Measure after load completes |

## Device or Simulator Differences

- Available units differ by hardware: `MLModel.availableComputeDevices` (subset of `MLComputeDevice.allComputeDevices` usable by Core ML). Simulator has no NE (measured) and the sample ML Program's ops were CPU-only there → profile on target devices; Performance reports run on any connected device.
- Scheme by unit: per-grouped-channel palettization suits the NE; int4 per-block quantization is optimized for Mac GPUs; W8A8 (int8 activations) gains latency on the NE with A17 Pro / M4. Gains are model- and hardware-dependent: measure on the target → `coreml-compression.md`.

## Memory Grows During Predictions

- Cause: unbounded concurrent async predictions keep many input/output sets alive; peak memory grows with in-flight count.
- Evidence: `xcrun xctrace record --template 'Allocations' --instrument 'Core ML' ...` → overlapping `Prediction` intervals tracking allocation growth.
- Fix: cap in-flight predictions; defer extra work, or drop it for live streams (Apple's example allows 2) → `coreml-deployment.md`.
- Don't: spin on `Task.yield()` waiting for a slot; pass `MLModel` / `MLFeatureProvider` into another actor (not `Sendable`; Swift 6 rejects with `sending 'model' risks causing data races`).

## Memory Spike at Load

- Weight size: `du -sh Model.mlpackage/Data/com.apple.CoreML/weights`.
- Compression shrinks disk; runtime memory depends on backend: some decompress fully before running (fp16 latency and footprint), others decompress on the fly. Measure with Allocations / VM Tracker.
- Palettization is typically best on the NE for runtime memory and latency.
- vs Float16 weights: 8-bit ≈ ½ (Apple: Stable Diffusion 8-bit palettized ≈ half), 4-bit ≈ ¼, plus lookup-table/scale overhead → `coreml-compression.md`.
- LLM-scale models → `core-ai.md`.

## Wrong Output on One Compute Unit

- Same model; CPU_ONLY correct, GPU/NE wrong → numeric precision in one op. Locate the first failing op with `MLModelComparator` (below; target = same model with `CPU_AND_NE`).
- Fix: keep that op in Float32 at conversion: `compute_precision=ct.transform.FP16ComputePrecision(op_selector=lambda op: op.op_type != "softmax")`. Selector returning `False` keeps the op FP32. Use a fresh source model per `ct.convert`: a MIL program reused after one conversion stays fp16 (measured). → `coreml-conversion.md`
- `allowLowPrecisionAccumulationOnGPU` defaults to `false`; if set `true`, unset it first.

## Accuracy Loss After Compression

Locate the damage first. Same tool for compute-unit bugs: swap `target`.

```python
import asyncio, numpy as np, coremltools as ct
from coremltools.models.ml_program.experimental.debugging_utils import MLModelComparator, compute_snr_and_psnr

reference = ct.models.MLModel("Model.mlpackage", compute_units=ct.ComputeUnit.CPU_ONLY)
target = ct.models.MLModel("Model_4bit.mlpackage", compute_units=ct.ComputeUnit.CPU_ONLY)
inputs = {"x": np.load("real_input.npy")}  # real sample, not noise
failing = asyncio.run(MLModelComparator(reference, target).find_failing_ops(
    inputs=inputs, compare_outputs=lambda op, ref, tgt: compute_snr_and_psnr(tgt.ravel(), ref.ravel())[1] >= 40.0))
print([(op.type, op.outputs[0].name) for op in failing])
```

- `compute_snr_and_psnr(noisy, reference)` → `(snr, psnr)`. **Flatten first**: it averages over `len()` (first axis), so a `(1, N)` output understates PSNR by 10·log10(N) dB (measured: 16.4 vs 40.5 dB at N=256) and flags healthy ops. SNR is unaffected.
- 40 dB is coremltools' own example threshold, not a standard; set it from your accuracy budget.
- Experimental module. Its docstring examples use `compute_unit=` and `compare_output=` with a two-argument callback; the real parameters are `compute_units=` and `compare_outputs=`, and the callback takes `(op, reference, target)`.

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 4-bit per-tensor palettization degrades | One 16-entry table for the whole tensor | `granularity="per_grouped_channel", group_size=16` (Apple's Stable Diffusion: most accuracy back, 1.29 → 1.3 GB) |
| Still degraded | Too few bits | More bits. Apple example (data-free): 8-bit quantization and 6-bit palettization preserved output, 4-bit showed artifacts, 2-bit failed |
| int4 quantization degrades | Per-channel scales too coarse | `granularity="per_block", block_size=32` |
| Data-free pruning degrades | Sparsity too high for data-free | Apple example: artifacts at 30%, broken at 40%; training-time pruning held through 75%. Next: SparseGPT calibration (`optimize.torch.layerwise_compression.LayerwiseCompressor` + `ModuleSparseGPTConfig`) or training-time |
| Fails at every granularity | Data-free limit at this bit-width | Calibration → QAT → `coreml-compression.md` |
| Size barely shrank | Tensors ≤ `weight_threshold` (default 2048 elements) are skipped silently (measured); `per_block` skips ops whose dim isn't divisible by `block_size` | List what qualifies: `cto.coreml.get_weights_metadata(model, weight_threshold=2048)` |
| Stacked compression didn't apply: size unchanged after a second pass (prune → quantize/palettize, palettize → quantize, quantize → prune) | The second `optimize.coreml` pass skips already-compressed weights unless `joint_compression=True`; no error, no warning (measured, coremltools 9.0: prune → `linear_quantize_weights` leaves only `constexpr_sparse_to_dense`) | Re-run the second pass with `joint_compression=True` (resulting ops per combination → `coreml-ref.md` Part 6) |
| `ValueError: … supported since iOS18 …` | Model converted below iOS 18 | → `coreml-compression.md` (Deployment target) |

Palettize / int4 / joint compression code → `coreml-ref.md` Part 6.

## Resources

**WWDC**: 2022-10027, 2023-10047, 2023-10049, 2024-10159, 2024-10161

**Docs**: /coreml/mlmodel, /coreml/mlcomputeplan-1w21n, /coreml/mlmodelconfiguration, /coreml/mloptimizationhints-swift.struct, /coreml/mlmodelerror-swift.struct, /coreml/downloading-and-compiling-a-model-on-the-user-s-device; coremltools guide (`opt-overview`, `typed-execution`, `flexible-inputs`)

axiom-ai--coreml-ref.content:
# Core ML API Reference

CoreML Swift API (checked against the iOS 27.1 SDK) + coremltools 9.0 Python index. Patterns and discipline → `coreml-deployment.md`; conversion decisions → `coreml-conversion.md`; compression decisions → `coreml-compression.md`; 27-cycle LLM runtime → `core-ai.md`.

Versions are iOS; same APIs on macOS/tvOS/watchOS/visionOS at the matching release unless noted. The 27.1 SDK adds no new CoreML API (Swift interface or headers).

## Part 1 — Model Lifecycle

### Loading

| API | Availability | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `MLModel.load(contentsOf:configuration:) async throws` | iOS 15 | preferred; `configuration` defaults to `MLModelConfiguration()`; URL = `.mlmodelc` |
| `MLModel.load(asset:configuration:) async throws` | iOS 16 | from `MLModelAsset`; no default configuration |
| `MLModel(contentsOf:configuration:) throws` | iOS 12 | synchronous — blocks caller |
| `MLModel.compileModel(at:) async throws -> URL` | iOS 16, not watchOS | `.mlmodel`/`.mlpackage` → temporary `.mlmodelc`; move it to keep it |
| `MLModel.compileModel(at:) throws -> URL` | not watchOS | sync; header marks it to-be-deprecated |

Specialization cache, invalidation, Core ML instrument load labels → `coreml-deployment.md` (Load, Cache, Pre-Warm).

### Asset types

| Type | What | Loaded at run time |
|---|---|---|
| `.mlmodel` | single-file spec: NeuralNetwork and other non-ML-Program types (an ML Program must save as `.mlpackage`) | no — compile first |
| `.mlpackage` | ML Program directory, weights stored separately | no — compile first |
| `.mlmodelc` | compiled; Xcode emits it for bundled models | yes |

### MLModelAsset

| API | Availability |
|---|---|
| `MLModelAsset(url:)` — compiled `.mlmodelc` | iOS 18 |
| `MLModelAsset(specification:)` — in-memory spec `Data` | iOS 16, not watchOS |
| `MLModelAsset(specification:blobMapping:)` | iOS 18, not watchOS |
| `try await asset.functionNames` / `modelDescription` / `modelDescription(of:)` | iOS 18 |

- `functionNames` = `[]` on a single-function model (measured, macOS 27.2)
- `modelDescription(of:)` with a name not in `functionNames` (including `"main"` on a single-function model) raises an uncaught `NSInvalidArgumentException` (`The specified function name: X is not among the available function names: [...]`) → **process abort**, not a throw; `do`/`catch` can't intercept it (measured, macOS 27.2). Guard with `functionNames.contains(name)`; single-function model → `modelDescription`

### MLModelConfiguration

| Property | Availability | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `computeUnits` | iOS 12 | Part 2 |
| `functionName: String?` | iOS 18 | `nil` → default function; multifunction: a name from `functionNames`; single-function ML Program: only `"main"`; NeuralNetwork: only `nil`; anything else → load throws (`coreml-diag.md` Load Failures) |
| `optimizationHints` (`MLOptimizationHints`) | iOS 17.4 | set in place: `configuration.optimizationHints.reshapeFrequency = .infrequent` |
| ↳ `reshapeFrequency` | iOS 17.4 | `.frequent` (default): fast shape switching, skips shape-specific optimization; `.infrequent`: stable shapes, re-optimizes on each shape change, faster predictions per seen shape |
| ↳ `specializationStrategy` | iOS 18 | `.default`; `.fastPrediction`: lower prediction latency "at the potential cost of specialization time, memory footprint, and the disk space usage of specialized artifacts" (SDK header) |
| `allowLowPrecisionAccumulationOnGPU` | iOS 13 | |
| `preferredMetalDevice` | iOS 13 | |
| `modelDisplayName` | iOS 16 | |
| `parameters: [MLParameterKey: Any]?` | iOS 13 | model/update parameters |

## Part 2 — Compute Availability

| `MLComputeUnits` | Availability | Runs on |
|---|---|---|
| `.all` | iOS 12 | CPU + GPU + Neural Engine |
| `.cpuAndNeuralEngine` | iOS 16 | excludes GPU |
| `.cpuAndGPU` | iOS 12 | excludes Neural Engine |
| `.cpuOnly` | iOS 12 | CPU |

`MLComputeDevice` (iOS 17, Swift enum, Sendable): `.cpu(MLCPUComputeDevice)`, `.gpu(MLGPUComputeDevice)`, `.neuralEngine(MLNeuralEngineComputeDevice)`.
- `MLModel.availableComputeDevices` → devices Core ML predictions can use
- `MLComputeDevice.allComputeDevices` → all hardware, including devices unavailable to Core ML
- GPU has no `name` → `gpu.metalDevice.name`; Neural Engine → `totalCoreCount`

```swift
import CoreML

func describeComputeDevices() -> [String] {
    MLModel.availableComputeDevices.map { device in
        switch device {
        case .cpu: "CPU"
        case .gpu(let gpu): "GPU \(gpu.metalDevice.name)"
        case .neuralEngine(let engine): "Neural Engine, \(engine.totalCoreCount) cores"
        @unknown default: "unknown"
        }
    }
}

func neuralEngineAvailable() -> Bool {
    MLModel.availableComputeDevices.contains { device in
        if case .neuralEngine = device { true } else { false }
    }
}
```

`MLComputePolicy` (iOS 18, `MLTensor` only): `.cpuOnly`, `.cpuAndGPU`, `MLComputePolicy(_ computeUnits: MLComputeUnits)` → `withMLTensorComputePolicy(_:_:)`.

## Part 3 — Prediction APIs

| Call | Availability | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `prediction(from:) throws` / `prediction(from:options:) throws` | iOS 11 | sync; not thread-safe |
| `prediction(from:options:) async throws` | iOS 17 | `options` defaults; Apple: thread-safe, best-effort cancellation |
| `predictions(fromBatch:) throws` | iOS 12 | batch |
| `predictions(from:options:) throws` | iOS 12 | batch with options; `predictions(from: batch)` alone → `missing argument for parameter 'options'` |
| `prediction(from:using:) throws` / `prediction(from:using:options:) throws` | iOS 18 | sync, stateful |
| `prediction(from:using:options:) async throws` | iOS 18 | async, stateful |
| `prediction(from: [String: MLTensor]) async throws -> [String: MLTensor]` | iOS 18 | all inputs/outputs must be multiarrays |
| `prediction(from: [String: MLTensor], using:) async throws` | iOS 18 | stateful tensor form |

`MLPredictionOptions.outputBackings` (iOS 16): `[featureName: CVPixelBuffer | MLMultiArray]` preallocated outputs; Core ML may ignore them (unknown name, unsupported model, batch mode) → compare output object identity to check; page-aligned `MLMultiArray` / IOSurface-backed pixel buffers perform best.

### State (iOS 18)

| API | Notes |
|---|---|
| `model.makeState() -> MLState` | zero-initialized buffers |
| `model.newState()` | unavailable in Swift — Apple's doc-comment examples still use it |
| `state.withMultiArray(for:_:)` | read/seed a named buffer; access only inside the closure |
| `state.withMultiArray(_:)` | deprecated |
| `modelDescription.stateDescriptionsByName` | declared states; `MLStateConstraint.bufferShape` / `dataType` |

Rules (SDK header): serialize predictions sharing one `MLState`, or behavior is undefined; never touch buffers while a prediction is in flight.

### Sendability (Swift 6)

| Type | Sendable |
|---|---|
| `MLModel`, `MLModelConfiguration`, `MLComputePlan`, `MLImageConstraint`, `any MLFeatureProvider`, `MLDictionaryFeatureProvider` | no |
| `MLState`, `MLTensor`, `MLShapedArray`, `MLShapedArraySlice`, `MLComputeDevice`, `MLComputePolicy`, `MLOptimizationHints` | yes |
| `MLSendableFeatureValue` (iOS 18) | yes — `MLSendableFeatureValue(_ value: MLFeatureValue)` failable; back via `MLFeatureValue(_:)` |
| `CVPixelBuffer` | no (conformance explicitly unavailable) |
| `CGImage` | yes |

Consequences and the three prediction shapes → `coreml-deployment.md`.

## Part 4 — MLTensor (iOS 18)

| Area | API |
|---|---|
| Create | `MLTensor(shape:scalars:scalarType:)`, `MLTensor(_ shapedArray:)`, `MLTensor(_ scalars:scalarType:)`, nested array literal, `MLTensor(zeros:scalarType:)` / `(ones:scalarType:)` / `(repeating:shape:)`, `(randomNormal:…)` / `(randomUniform:…)`, `(rangeFrom:to:by:)`, `(linearSpaceFrom:through:count:)`, `(concatenating:alongAxis:)`, `(stacking:alongAxis:)` |
| Inspect | `shape`, `rank`, `scalarCount`, `scalarType`, `isScalar` |
| Math | `+ - * / %` (tensor or scalar, broadcasting), `matmul`, `pow`, `exp`, `log`, `squareRoot`, `rsqrt`, `abs`, …, `softmax(alongAxis:)` (default last axis), `clamped(to:)`; free functions `pointwiseMin(_:_:)` / `pointwiseMax(_:_:)` (scalar overloads iOS 26) |
| Reduce | `sum`, `mean`, `min`, `max`, `product`, `all`, `any` (`alongAxes:keepRank:`); `argmax()` / `argmin()` (flattened, `Int32`), `argmax(alongAxis:keepRank:)` |
| Compare / logic | `.== .!= .> .>= .< .<=` → Bool tensor; `.& .| .^ .!`; `replacing(with:where:)` |
| Index | `t[0]`, `t[0..<2, 1..<3]`, `t[..., 0]` (unbounded = `...`), `.newAxis`, `.squeezeAxis`, `.range(_:stride:)` |
| Shape | `reshaped(to:)`, `flattened()`, `expandingShape(at:)`, `squeezingShape()`, `transposed(permutation:)`, `concatenated(with:alongAxis:)`, `split(count:)` / `split(sizes:)`, `unstacked`, `tiled(multiples:)`, `padded(forSizes:…)`, `resized(to:method:)`, `cast(to:)` |
| LLM helpers | `topK(_ k:)` → `(values, indices: Int32)` along last axis; `argsort`; `gathering(atIndices:alongAxis:)` (Int32 indices); `bandPart(lowerBandCount:upperBandCount:)` (causal masks); `cumulativeSum` |
| Materialize | `await t.shapedArray(of: Float.self)` — required before reading scalars |
| Device | `withMLTensorComputePolicy(.cpuAndGPU) { … }` (sync and async overloads, task-local) |

Absent — common wrong guesses: `multinomial(numSamples:)`, `topK(k:)` (label), `t[.all, 0]` (→ `t[..., 0]`).

```swift
import CoreML

func tensorBasics() async -> [Float] {
    let x = MLTensor(shape: [2, 3], scalars: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], scalarType: Float.self)
    let fromShaped = MLTensor(MLShapedArray<Float>(scalars: [1, 2, 3, 4], shape: [2, 2]))
    let nested = MLTensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]])
    let columnIndices = MLTensor([2, 0], scalarType: Int32.self)

    let y = (x + Float(1)) * Float(2)
    let mean = y.mean()
    let rowSums = y.sum(alongAxes: 1)
    let clipped = y.replacing(with: Float(0), where: y .> mean)

    let firstRow = x[0]
    let firstColumn = x[..., 0]
    let corner = x[0..<2, 1..<3]
    let batched = x.expandingShape(at: 0)
    let picked = x.gathering(atIndices: columnIndices, alongAxis: 1)
    let product = fromShaped.matmul(nested)

    _ = (rowSums, firstRow, firstColumn, corner, batched, picked, product)
    return await clipped.shapedArray(of: Float.self).scalars
}
```

Typed scalars (`Float(1)`) → scalar overload. Bare `1` → `MLTensor(integerLiteral:)`, an `Int32` tensor, through the tensor–tensor overload (checked in SIL). Sampling example → `coreml-deployment.md`.

## Part 5 — coremltools Conversion Index (Python)

Decisions (format, trace vs export, parity) → `coreml-conversion.md`.

| Symbol | Notes |
|---|---|
| `ct.convert(model, source=, inputs=, outputs=, classifier_config=, minimum_deployment_target=, convert_to=, compute_precision=, skip_model_load=, compute_units=, package_dir=, debug=, pass_pipeline=, states=)` | 9.0 signature |
| `ct.TensorType(name=, shape=, dtype=, default_value=)` | |
| `ct.ImageType(name=, shape=, scale=, bias=, color_layout=, channel_first=, grayscale_use_uint8=)` | `grayscale_use_uint8` needs iOS 17 target |
| `ct.RangeDim(lower_bound=1, upper_bound=-1, default=None, symbol=None)` | bounded dynamic dim |
| `ct.EnumeratedShapes(shapes, default=None)` | fixed set of shapes |
| `ct.StateType(wrapped_type=ct.TensorType(shape=, dtype=np.float16), name=)` | rules → `coreml-conversion.md` (Stateful models) |
| `ct.target.iOS13` … `iOS18`, `iOS26` | what each unlocks → Part 9 |
| `ct.precision.FLOAT16` / `FLOAT32` | |
| `ct.ComputeUnit.ALL` / `CPU_AND_GPU` / `CPU_ONLY` / `CPU_AND_NE` | Python-side load/predict |
| `ct.models.MLModel(path, skip_model_load=, compute_units=, function_name=, optimization_hints=)` | `function_name` picks a multifunction function |

## Part 6 — Compression Index (coremltools.optimize)

Decisions (PTQ vs calibration vs QAT, bit-width ladder, compute-unit fit) → `coreml-compression.md`.

### `coremltools.optimize.coreml` — on the `.mlpackage`

| Config | Defaults | Function |
|---|---|---|
| `OpPalettizerConfig(mode="kmeans", nbits=, granularity="per_tensor", group_size=32, channel_axis=, cluster_dim=1, enable_per_channel_scale=False, num_kmeans_workers=1, lut_function=, weight_threshold=2048)` | | `palettize_weights(model, config, joint_compression=False)` |
| `OpLinearQuantizerConfig(mode="linear_symmetric", dtype="int8", granularity="per_channel", block_size=32, weight_threshold=2048)` | modes `linear` / `linear_symmetric` | `linear_quantize_weights(model, config, joint_compression=False)` |
| `OpMagnitudePrunerConfig(target_sparsity=, block_size=, n_m_ratio=, dim=, weight_threshold=2048)` / `OpThresholdPrunerConfig` | | `prune_weights(model, config, joint_compression=False)` |
| same `OpLinearQuantizerConfig` | 8-bit activations only; runs the model on sample data | `linear_quantize_activations(model, config, sample_data)` → pair with weight quantization for W8A8 |

- Wrap configs in `OptimizationConfig(global_config=, op_type_configs=, op_name_configs=)`
- `weight_threshold`: only tensors with more than this many elements are compressed
- `mode="kmeans"` needs scikit-learn (`kmeans1d` replaces it only for fp16 tensors of ≥10,000 elements, if installed) → otherwise `ModuleNotFoundError: scikit-learn is required for k-means quantization.`
- **Stacking passes needs `joint_compression=True` on the second pass.** Without it the second pass leaves already-compressed weights untouched, no error, no warning (measured, coremltools 9.0): prune → `linear_quantize_weights` leaves ops `{constexpr_sparse_to_dense}` only; with the flag → `{constexpr_sparse_blockwise_shift_scale, constexpr_sparse_to_dense}`. Same skip for prune → palettize (joint → `constexpr_lut_to_sparse`), palettize → quantize, quantize → prune. Palettize → quantize joint needs `granularity="per_tensor"` (else `NotImplementedError`). Joint needs iOS 18 target
- iOS 18-gated schemes and their `ValueError` → `coreml-compression.md` (Deployment target)
- Also: `decompress_weights`, `get_weights_metadata`

```python
import coremltools as ct
import coremltools.optimize as cto

model = ct.models.MLModel("Model.mlpackage", skip_model_load=True)

palettized = cto.coreml.palettize_weights(model, cto.coreml.OptimizationConfig(
    global_config=cto.coreml.OpPalettizerConfig(mode="kmeans", nbits=4, granularity="per_grouped_channel", group_size=16)))
palettized.save("Model-palettized.mlpackage")

int4 = cto.coreml.linear_quantize_weights(model, cto.coreml.OptimizationConfig(
    global_config=cto.coreml.OpLinearQuantizerConfig(dtype="int4", granularity="per_block", block_size=32)))

pruned = cto.coreml.prune_weights(model, cto.coreml.OptimizationConfig(
    global_config=cto.coreml.OpMagnitudePrunerConfig(target_sparsity=0.5)))
sparse_int8 = cto.coreml.linear_quantize_weights(pruned, cto.coreml.OptimizationConfig(
    global_config=cto.coreml.OpLinearQuantizerConfig(dtype="int8")), joint_compression=True)
```

`Model.mlpackage` converted with `minimum_deployment_target` ≥ `ct.target.iOS18`.

### `coremltools.optimize.torch` — on the PyTorch model (needs PyTorch)

| Class | Module | Kind | Lifecycle |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DKMPalettizer` | `palettization` | QAT | `prepare()` → train, `step()` per step → `finalize()` |
| `LinearQuantizer` | `quantization` | QAT | same |
| `MagnitudePruner` | `pruning` | QAT | same |
| `SKMPalettizer` | `palettization` | calibration PTQ | `compute_sensitivity` / `compress` |
| `PostTrainingPalettizer` / `PostTrainingQuantizer` | `palettization` / `quantization` | data-free PTQ | `compress()` |
| `LayerwiseCompressor` + `GPTQ` (quantization) / `SparseGPT` (pruning) | `layerwise_compression` (not `pruning`) | calibration PTQ | `compress(dataloader, device)` — `device` is required |

- Config objects are `XConfig(global_config=ModuleXConfig(...))` or `XConfig.from_dict({"global_config": {...}})`; a raw dict passed as `global_config=` fails validation
- `LayerwiseCompressorConfig`: sequential models only; `layers=None` → all immediate children; `calibration_nsamples` default 128; `global_config` dict needs `"algorithm": "gptq"` or `"sparse_gpt"`
- Compression metadata travels in the state dict (`_COREML_` keys) and is read by the converter

```python
from coremltools.optimize.torch.palettization import DKMPalettizer, DKMPalettizerConfig
from coremltools.optimize.torch.layerwise_compression import LayerwiseCompressor, LayerwiseCompressorConfig

config = DKMPalettizerConfig.from_dict({"global_config": {"n_bits": 4}})
palettizer = DKMPalettizer(model, config)
prepared = palettizer.prepare()
for epoch in range(num_epochs):
    train_one_epoch(prepared, train_loader)
    palettizer.step()
palettized = palettizer.finalize()

sparse_config = LayerwiseCompressorConfig.from_dict({
    "global_config": {"algorithm": "sparse_gpt", "target_sparsity": 0.5},
    "calibration_nsamples": 128,
})
pruned = LayerwiseCompressor(model, sparse_config).compress(calibration_loader, device="cpu")
```

`model`, `train_one_epoch`, `train_loader`, `num_epochs` and `calibration_loader` are your PyTorch objects.

## Part 7 — Multifunction Models

| Side | API |
|---|---|
| Python | `ct.utils.MultiFunctionDescriptor(model_path=None)`; `.add_function(model_path, src_function_name, target_function_name)`; `.add_model(path)`; `.remove_function(name)`; `.default_function_name` (required before save) |
| Python | `ct.utils.save_multifunction(desc, destination_path)` → spec version forced to iOS 18; shared weights deduplicated |
| Python | `ct.models.MLModel(path, function_name="…")` |
| Swift | `MLModelConfiguration.functionName`; `MLModelAsset(url:)` + `try await asset.functionNames`; `modelDescription(of:)` — name must be in `functionNames`, else process abort (Part 1) |
| Xcode | model preview lists functions above the inputs |

Pitfalls: `MultiFunctionDescriptor` is not in `ct.models`; the 9.0 docstring's `source_function_name=` keyword → `TypeError`. Merge and load code → `coreml-deployment.md`.

## Part 8 — Performance Profiling

`MLComputePlan` (iOS 17.4; not Sendable): `load(contentsOf:configuration:)` / `load(asset:configuration:)` — `configuration` required; URL = `.mlmodelc` (an `.mlpackage` aborts the process → `coreml-diag.md` Red Flags). `modelStructure` is an `MLModelStructure` enum (`.program`, `.neuralNetwork`, `.pipeline`, `.unsupported`), not a list of operations. Per op: `deviceUsage(for:)` → `.preferred` / `.supported`; `estimatedCost(of:)` → `.weight`, the op's fraction (0–1) of total model execution. Walk code → `coreml-diag.md` First Steps.

NeuralNetwork models: `case .neuralNetwork(let network)` → `network.layers` → `deviceUsage(for: layer)` (no cost estimate). `MLModelStructure.load(contentsOf:)` (iOS 17.4) gives the structure without a plan.

| Tool | Shows |
|---|---|
| Xcode model → Performance → + → device + compute units → Run Test | load/prediction times, compute-unit split; per-op estimated time and device support; hover an unsupported op for the reason; export and compare reports |
| Instruments: any template + the Core ML instrument (`xctrace record --instrument 'Core ML'`; Xcode 27.1 ships no Core ML template) — command → `coreml-diag.md` First Steps | load events (labels → `coreml-deployment.md`), predictions, compute-unit activity; add the Neural Engine, GPU, Allocations instruments |

## Part 9 — Deployment Targets

| Target | Core ML runtime | coremltools `minimum_deployment_target` unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| iOS 15 | async `MLModel.load(contentsOf:)`, `MLShapedArray` | ML Program (`.mlpackage`) |
| iOS 16 | `compileModel(at:) async`, `.cpuAndNeuralEngine`, `MLModelAsset(specification:)`, `outputBackings` | weight compression ops: per-tensor palettization, per-channel int8 quantization, sparsity |
| iOS 17 | async `prediction(from:)`, `MLComputeDevice` / `availableComputeDevices` | activation quantization (W8A8), uint8 grayscale image input |
| iOS 17.4 | `MLComputePlan`, `MLModelStructure`, `optimizationHints.reshapeFrequency` | — |
| iOS 18 | `MLTensor`, `MLState` / `makeState()`, `functionName`, `MLModelAsset(url:)`, `specializationStrategy`, `MLSendableFeatureValue` | `StateType`, fused SDPA, `per_grouped_channel` palettization, `per_block` and int4 quantization, joint compression, multifunction |
| iOS 26 | `Int8` `MLShapedArray` / `MLMultiArray` scalars; scalar `pointwiseMin` / `pointwiseMax` | int8 model inputs/outputs |
| 27 | no new CoreML Swift API; background-inference entitlement `OS27` (`coreml-deployment.md`) | — |

`minimum_deployment_target`: at least `ct.target.iOS18` (states, SDPA, modern compression); use your app's minimum OS (`ct.target.iOS26` for a 26+ app). The iOS 26 row (int8 inputs/outputs) needs `iOS26`.

## Part 10 — Conversion Pass Pipelines

| `pass_pipeline=` | Use |
|---|---|
| default (`ct.PassPipeline.DEFAULT`) | normal conversion |
| `ct.PassPipeline.DEFAULT_PALETTIZATION` | source model already has palettized weights → emit compressed format |
| `ct.PassPipeline.DEFAULT_PRUNING` | source model has sparse weights → emit sparse format |
| `ct.PassPipeline.CLEANUP` | cleanup passes only (const elimination, dead code) |
| `ct.PassPipeline.EMPTY` | no graph passes |
| `ct.PassPipeline()` + `.remove_passes({"common::fuse_conv_batchnorm"})` / `.set_options("common::const_elimination", {"skip_const_by_size": "1e6"})` | custom |

axiom-ai--coreml-training.name: axiom-ai--coreml-training
axiom-ai--coreml-training.description: Two distinct on-device/on-Mac training paths that developers constantly conflate:
axiom-ai--coreml-training.content:
# Core ML Training & Personalization

Two distinct on-device/on-Mac training paths that developers constantly conflate:

- **Create ML** — train a *new* Core ML model from scratch (or via transfer learning).
- **`MLUpdateTask`** — *personalize* an already-deployed model on the user's own data, at runtime.

Both produce or update a Core ML model. Neither has anything to do with fine-tuning Apple's Foundation Models (that's `foundation-models-adapters.md`) or converting an existing model (that's `coreml-conversion.md`).

## When to Use

- You want to train an image/sound/text/tabular model without writing a training loop → Create ML.
- You want each user's copy of a model to adapt to *their* data on-device → `MLUpdateTask`.
- You started building on-device personalization and hit a wall because your model is an `.mlpackage` → read the NN-spec limitation below before going further.

---

## Create ML — train from scratch

Two surfaces, same engine:

- **Create ML app** (macOS) — no-code GUI. Drag in training data, pick a template, train, export.
- **CreateML framework** (`import CreateML`) — programmatic training.

**Availability is per-type, not blanket-macOS.** `MLImageClassifier` and `MLSoundClassifier` train on iOS 15+/iPadOS/visionOS as well as macOS; others (e.g. `MLRecommender`) remain macOS-only. Don't assume "Create ML = Mac-only" — check the specific type.

### Model types (CreateML framework)

Image (`MLImageClassifier`, `MLObjectDetector`), sound (`MLSoundClassifier`), text (`MLTextClassifier`, `MLWordTagger`), pose/action (`MLHandPoseClassifier`, `MLActionClassifier`, `MLHandActionClassifier`), style (`MLStyleTransfer`), tabular (`MLRegressor`, `MLClassifier` — backed by boosted-tree / linear / random-forest), and `MLRecommender` (macOS-only).

> The Create ML *app* also offers a Tabular/Time-Series flow, but there is no confirmed `MLTimeSeriesForecaster` type in the framework — use the app for that workflow.

### Programmatic shape

```swift
import CreateML
import Foundation

@concurrent
func trainImageClassifier(labeledImagesAt trainingURL: URL, exportTo modelURL: URL) async throws {
    let data = MLImageClassifier.DataSource.labeledDirectories(at: trainingURL)
    let classifier = try MLImageClassifier(trainingData: data)  // synchronous — blocks this thread until training ends
    try classifier.write(to: modelURL)                          // exports a .mlmodel
}
```

- Training data: **directory-of-label-folders** for image classifiers; `MLDataTable(contentsOf:)` from CSV/JSON for tabular.
- The throwing `init(trainingData:parameters:)` is **synchronous and blocking**. For UI apps use `makeTrainingSession(...)` / the async `train(...)` API and report progress; resume from a checkpoint with `init(checkpoint:)`.
- Export produces a **`.mlmodel`** (attach `MLModelMetadata` for author/version/description).
- Training is GPU-accelerated on Apple Silicon (Metal).

---

## `MLUpdateTask` — on-device personalization

`MLUpdateTask` retrains the **last few updatable layers** of an already-deployed model on user-specific data, then saves an updated `.mlmodelc` to disk. This is per-user personalization at runtime — not training from scratch.

```swift
import CoreML

nonisolated func personalize(modelAt compiledModelURL: URL, with userData: any MLBatchProvider, savingTo updatedModelURL: URL) throws {
    let task = try MLUpdateTask(
        forModelAt: compiledModelURL,
        trainingData: userData,
        configuration: MLModelConfiguration(),
        completionHandler: { context in
            do {
                try context.model.write(to: updatedModelURL)   // persist the personalized model
            } catch {
                print("MLUpdateTask: saving \(updatedModelURL.lastPathComponent) failed: \(error)")
            }
        }
    )
    task.resume()
}
```

- `nonisolated` matters under `-default-isolation MainActor`: unannotated, the non-`Sendable` completion closure becomes main-actor-isolated and carries a runtime executor check (SIL) → traps if Core ML calls it off the main actor.
- Initializers come in `completionHandler:` and `progressHandlers:` variants (with/without `configuration:`); `MLUpdateContext` carries the updated model.
- Loss functions: **categorical cross-entropy, MSE**. Optimizers: **SGD, Adam**.
- Available since iOS 13.

### ⚠️ The NN-spec-only limitation (read before building)

**`MLUpdateTask` only works with NeuralNetwork-spec models — NOT ML Program (`.mlpackage`) models from modern PyTorch/TensorFlow conversion.** You make a model updatable with coremltools `NeuralNetworkBuilder.make_updatable(layer_names)`, which supports **only `innerProduct` (fully-connected) and `convolution` layers**, and exists only for the NN-spec format.

This is the single most important fact about on-device personalization, and the reason it's rarely used in new projects: if your pipeline converts a PyTorch/TF model the modern way, you get an `.mlpackage` that **cannot** be personalized with `MLUpdateTask`. Developers routinely discover this after building most of the pipeline. Surface it on day one:

- Modern conversion (`coremltools.convert` → `.mlpackage`) → **no `MLUpdateTask`**.
- On-device personalization required → you must build/convert to an **NN-spec** model and call `make_updatable()` — accepting NN-spec's constraints and legacy status.

### When `MLUpdateTask` is still the right tool

- A legacy NN-spec model you already ship.
- Very constrained per-user personalization (last-layer adaptation) where the NN-spec limitation matches the task.
- The personalization must stay **on-device** for privacy and run without a server round-trip.

If you need richer adaptation than last-layer updates, `MLUpdateTask` is the wrong tool — retrain with Create ML (server-side or on-Mac) and ship updated models, or rethink the architecture.

---

## Boundary recap

| Path | Trains | Output | Runs |
|------|--------|--------|------|
| Create ML | A new model from scratch / transfer learning | `.mlmodel` | macOS / iOS (per type) at build time |
| `MLUpdateTask` | Last updatable layers of an NN-spec model | Updated `.mlmodelc` | On device, at runtime, per-user |
| FM adapter | Apple's frozen on-device LLM (LoRA) | `.fmadapter` | See `foundation-models-adapters.md` |
| coremltools convert | Nothing (format conversion) | `.mlpackage` | See `coreml-conversion.md` |

## Anti-Rationalization

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I'll personalize my converted `.mlpackage` with `MLUpdateTask`" | `MLUpdateTask` is **NN-spec only**. ML Program models can't be updated — you'd have to rebuild as NN-spec. Check this *before* building the pipeline. |
| "Create ML is just for the Mac app / prototyping" | The `CreateML` framework trains programmatically, and image/sound classifiers train on iOS/iPadOS/visionOS too. |
| "`MLUpdateTask` can retrain my whole model on-device" | It updates the *last* fully-connected/convolutional layers only. It's last-layer personalization, not full retraining. |
| "Personalization and fine-tuning an LLM are the same thing" | `MLUpdateTask` personalizes a small Core ML model; fine-tuning Apple's LLM is FM adapter training (`foundation-models-adapters.md`). Entirely different toolchains. |
| "Training blocks? I'll call `init(trainingData:)` on the main thread" | The synchronous initializer blocks. Use the async training session and report progress, or run off the main thread. |

## Resources

**WWDC**: 2018-703, 2019-430, 2019-704 (`MLUpdateTask` / on-device personalization), 2021-10037, 2024-10183

**Docs**: /createml, /createml/mlimageclassifier, /coreml/mlupdatetask, /coreml/mlupdatecontext — plus coremltools `NeuralNetworkBuilder.make_updatable` (apple.github.io/coremltools)

**Skills**: coreml-conversion (NN-spec vs ML Program), coreml-compression (shrink trained models), `skills/coreml-deployment.md` (deploy), foundation-models-adapters (fine-tune Apple's LLM, not a Core ML model), axiom-concurrency (off-main-thread training)
